rationale: This article is a conceptual/foresight piece proposing Multi-Utility Service Companies (MUSCos) to achieve resource-efficient, sustainable integrated infrastructure operation. It explicitly states that it presents 'new insights and ideas' rather than empirical primary research or a systematic review (failing Criterion 3, E05), does not specifically examine household water or sanitation service access outcomes (failing Criterion 4), and does not analyse a legal or administrative access-governing mechanism under Criterion 2.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Broad infrastructure governance and Multi-Utility Service Company (MUSCo) institutional configurations engage the literal governance/institutional wording of plain Criterion 2, whereas no specific legal or administrative rule governing household water/sanitation access is examined under narrow Criterion 2; however, both readings result in exclusion because the paper is a conceptual perspective piece with no empirical evidence or systematic synthesis (E05) and focuses on resource efficiency across general infrastructure rather than water/sanitation access outcomes.

evidence_quotes.quote: This article presents new insights and ideas generated by considering the challenge of the transition towards a MUSCo infrastructure.
To achieve long-term sustainability, infrastructure needs to be designed and operated to provide essential service delivery at radically decreased levels of resource use.
Towards resource-efficient and service-oriented integrated infrastructure operation
